questions: How far does the bus go in one hour, and how far after two hours?
What does the 60 in 60 km/h count?
segments.say: Speed is distance per hour. Show the bus covering 60 km in the first hour, then 120 km after two hours and 180 km after three, and name the idea: the 60 counts kilometres per hour. Keep your student notes open at the speed definition for this scene.

questions: How far does the bus go in the half hour at the end?
What multiplication gives the whole distance, and how do the parts check it?
segments.say: 60 km/h for 2.5 hours. Build the distance in parts first - 60 km, then 120 km, then a half-hour step of 30 km - before landing the multiplication: distance = speed × time, so 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

questions: How far has the bus gone after half an hour?
Why does half the time give half the distance?
segments.say: Watch out: speed is not distance. Put the half-hour journey on the board: at 60 km/h for half an hour the bus reaches 30 km, because half the time means half the distance. Now try the rate questions on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: What is the distance at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours, and what are the three formulas in the family?
What goes wrong if we read a speed as a distance already travelled?
segments.say: The takeaway. Land the family: distance = speed × time, speed = distance ÷ time, time = distance ÷ speed. Finish by taking the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits exactly this trap.
segments.watchFor: 60 km/h means the bus has travelled 60 km. Listen and look for it in pair talk and on the worksheet: any answer of 60 km for the half-hour journey shows the trap - send them back to scene s3 and to the correct turn: Speed is distance per hour: after half an hour at 60 km/h the bus has gone 30 km, not 60.
